prompt: What do you hand App Engine standard to deploy the storefront?
hint: No machine, no container.

choices.text: A container image pushed to a registry
choices.why: That is Cloud Run, or App Engine flexible with a custom runtime.

choices.text: A machine image built with Packer
choices.why: There is no machine in anything you write.

choices.text: Source code and an app.yaml describing it
choices.why: Right. Google builds, runs and scales it.

choices.text: A zip of the virtual environment
choices.why: Google installs from requirements.txt.

prompt: The storefront answered "version local" on the laptop. Why?
hint: Which variable did the page read?

choices.text: GAE_VERSION is unset outside App Engine
choices.why: Right. The code falls back to local.

choices.text: gunicorn names every version local
choices.why: gunicorn sets no such variable.

choices.text: app.yaml was not found, so a default was used
choices.why: app.yaml is read by Google's build, not by the page.

choices.text: Flask reports local when PORT is 8081
choices.why: The port has nothing to do with it.

prompt: Match each line of the storefront's app.yaml to what it decides.
hint: Four lines of decision.

pairs.right: The language and version Google builds for
The command that starts the server

prompt: App Engine sets the variable ___ before running the entrypoint, and gunicorn binds to it.
hint: Cloud Run sets the same one.

prompt: gcloud app deploy stopped with "You do not currently have an active account selected". What does that tell you about the folder?
hint: When does gcloud check the account?

choices.text: That app.yaml is valid, since gcloud read it first
choices.why: The account check comes before anything is read.

choices.text: That the region southamerica-east1 is not offered
choices.why: No region was asked about.

choices.text: That requirements.txt is missing
choices.why: Nothing was built, so nothing was missed.

choices.text: Nothing: gcloud refused before reading it
choices.why: Right. The refusal happens on the laptop, first.

prompt: An F1 costs 0.05 USD an instance-hour after 28 free hours a day. One F1 runs all day, every day. What does a day cost?
hint: A day has 24 hours.

prompt: Which scaling suits a back-office tool used twice a day?
hint: It should start on demand and let go afterwards.

choices.text: Manual, with one instance always running
choices.why: It would run all day for two visits.

choices.text: Basic, on a B class
choices.why: Right. It starts on the first request and stops when idle.

choices.text: Manual, on an F class
choices.why: F classes are for automatic scaling.

choices.text: Basic, on an F class
choices.why: Basic scaling uses B classes.

prompt: Order these from the outermost to the innermost.
hint: Follow the figure inwards.

prompt: Why split traffic between v1 and v2 by cookie rather than at random?
hint: Think of one person making several requests.

choices.text: Cookies make the split exactly 90 and 10
choices.why: The proportion is the same either way; consistency is the point.

choices.text: Random splitting is billed per request
choices.why: Splitting has no price of its own.

choices.text: It keeps one person on one version across requests
choices.why: Right. Two versions that disagree must not alternate for one visitor.

choices.text: App Engine refuses random splits on the default service
choices.why: Random is one of the three options.

prompt: How do you test v2 before it receives any traffic?
hint: Each version keeps its own address.

choices.text: Open v2-dot-planner-dev.rj.r.appspot.com
choices.why: Right. The version answers there with no share of the split.

choices.text: Deploy it to a second project first
choices.why: Possible, but the version already has an address of its own.

choices.text: Split 1% to it and watch the logs
choices.why: That gives it traffic.

choices.text: Run it with manual scaling and zero instances
choices.why: With zero instances nothing answers.

prompt: Instance classes that begin with the letter ___ are for automatic scaling.
hint: The other letter is B.

prompt: Flexible costs 0.0526 USD per vCPU-hour and 0.0071 per GiB-hour. What do two instances of 1 vCPU and 2 GiB cost for 730 hours?
What does env: flex change about where the code runs?
hint: Containers, on machines.

choices.text: It runs in the same sandbox, with more memory
choices.why: Flexible leaves the sandbox entirely.

choices.text: It runs on Cloud Run under App Engine's name
choices.why: Cloud Run is a different product, which Google now recommends instead.

choices.text: It runs on your own machines, managed remotely
choices.why: The machines are Google's.

choices.text: It runs in a container on Compute Engine machines App Engine manages
choices.why: Right. That is what made any language possible.

prompt: Which setting makes a flexible service unable to cost nothing on a quiet day?
hint: It has a floor above zero.

choices.text: resources.cpu
choices.why: Size sets the price per hour, not whether hours run.

choices.text: min_num_instances, which cannot be zero
choices.why: Right. At least one machine always runs.

choices.text: max_num_instances
choices.why: A ceiling does not force anything to run.

choices.text: runtime_config
choices.why: It picks the operating system and version.

prompt: A team inherits a working flexible app and proposes moving it to Cloud Run "because flex is deprecated". What is the accurate version of that argument?
hint: What does the lesson say about an inherited app?

choices.text: Flex stops serving at the end of the year
choices.why: The lesson names no such date.

choices.text: Flex cannot run Python 3.12
choices.why: The lesson's app.yaml asks for 3.12.

choices.text: It keeps working; Cloud Run adds scale to zero and per-request billing
choices.why: Right. The case is cost and speed, not an end date.

choices.text: Cloud Run is cheaper at every load
choices.why: Lesson 22 shows loads where it is not.

prompt: In app.yaml, runtime: ___ makes App Engine build the Dockerfile in the folder.
hint: Any language gets in this way.

prompt: A team created the App Engine application in the wrong region. What does it take to fix?
hint: The region is chosen once.

choices.text: A new project and a migration
choices.why: Right. One application per project, in one region.

choices.text: Changing location_id and applying again
choices.why: The region cannot be changed.

choices.text: A support ticket to move it
choices.why: Google documents it as permanent.

choices.text: Deleting the default service and recreating it
choices.why: The default service cannot be deleted.

prompt: A Python 3 app needs a cache. What does the lesson recommend?
hint: Bundled services belong to the past.

choices.text: App Engine's bundled Memcache, built into the runtime
choices.why: Second-generation runtimes leave it out by default.

choices.text: A dictionary at module level
choices.why: Each instance would hold its own, and lose it when stopped.

choices.text: Cloud Tasks, which stores values by key
choices.why: Cloud Tasks is a queue, not a cache.

choices.text: Memorystore, the standalone product
choices.why: Right. Google recommends the standalone products.

prompt: Why did the plan of google_app_engine_application need only location_id?
hint: One application per project.

choices.text: The name comes from app.yaml at plan time
choices.why: Terraform does not read app.yaml.

choices.text: The project is the application's identity, and only the region is a choice
choices.why: Right. There is nothing else to name.

choices.text: The provider fills the region from CLOUDSDK_COMPUTE_REGION
choices.why: The file sets location_id explicitly.

choices.text: Services and versions are created in the same resource
choices.why: Those come from deploys, not from this resource.

prompt: Which situations does the lesson call a good fit for App Engine standard? Choose all that apply.
hint: Small and conventional.

choices.text: A small internal tool idle most of the day
choices.why: Right; the free hours cover it.

choices.text: A team that wants no container or registry
choices.why: Right; source and app.yaml only.

choices.text: An app that must run in two regions
choices.why: One region per project.

choices.text: A program that needs a library no runtime has
choices.why: That is a container, so Cloud Run.

prompt: Under automatic scaling in the standard environment, how many minutes may one request take?
hint: The lesson names it.

prompt: Put the release of storefront v2 in a safe order.
hint: Test before traffic, then a little traffic.
items: Move all traffic to v2 once it holds

prompt: The shop wants its storefront served from São Paulo and Iowa with App Engine. What is the smallest arrangement that works?
hint: How many regions may one application have?

choices.text: One application with two services, one per region
choices.why: All services share the application's one region.

choices.text: One application with versions pinned to regions
choices.why: Versions do not choose regions.

choices.text: Two projects, each with its own application
choices.why: Right. One application per project, one region each.

choices.text: One application in the global location
choices.why: App Engine has no global location.
